summary_of_threads_started_this_week:
Emerging quantum computing threats have prompted the development of advanced post-quantum migration strategies for cryptocurrencies, including mechanisms such as "Quantum Landmines," staked and Sats auctions, which employ game theory and incentive structures to deter theft of legacy coins and adaptively respond to attacker behavior after Q-day. These proposals, detailed by multiple contributors, emphasize creative defensive economics and seek to transform quantum vulnerabilities into self-policing opportunities, as outlined in the [source discussion](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/40a9f73d-481f-47e6-a64b-acfb2c7f4fa8n@googlegroups.com/T/#u#mf34978d175c7e432f8b66d7e6d88b977c83da474) and the [Wikipedia article on Dollar Auctions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dollar_auction).

In digital signature security, recent work—including contributions from Sjors Provoost and Pieter Wuille—proposes an anti-exfiltration protocol to prevent hardware wallets from leaking private seeds through manipulated signature nonces, with ongoing efforts to standardize these measures in Bitcoin Improvement Proposals and implement them across wallet hardware. Draft specifications, test vectors, and resources are available at [AvilaLabs/anti-exfil](https://github.com/AvilaLabs/anti-exfil) and [anti-exfil.avilalabs.org](https://anti-exfil.avilalabs.org), but formal cryptographic review remains pending.

The Tapleaf 0xc2 initiative introduces a suite of proposals to restore and extend Bitcoin Script, enabling advanced features like general covenants, transaction introspection, and reusable macros while carefully managing computational costs and backward compatibility. Comprehensive technical details and reference implementations can be accessed via [BIP 440](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-0440.mediawiki), [BIP 441](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-0441.mediawiki), and related documents, with the [Bitcoin Core fork](https://github.com/bitcoin-gsr/bitcoin/tree/gsr) providing a testing ground for these enhancements.

Additional discussions address practical issues such as full OP_RETURN value pruning in nodes ([satd 0.7.0](https://github.com/epochbtc/satd/releases/tag/v0.7.0)), formal verification of BIP340 batch signature soundness ([bip340-batch-verify](https://github.com/dni/bip340-batch-verify)), decentralized identity anchored in Bitcoin via the Tulip protocol ([tuliproot.com](https://tuliproot.com/)), and ongoing challenges in wallet address compatibility and user experience, highlighting the need for improved [compatibility databases](https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/Bech32_adoption) and transparent communication across the ecosystem.

new_threads_this_week.title: Quantum Landmines and Vulnerable Coin Auctions
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Multiple strategies use economic incentives to protect legacy cryptocurrency from post-quantum attacks.  - Quantum Landmines and Staked Auctions penalize attackers and reward defenders through collateral-based mechanisms.  - Sats Auction introduces competitive bidding, further increasing risks for attackers and opportunities for legitimate owners.

new_threads_this_week.title: Draft BIPs: anti-exfil signing for BIP340 and ECDSA, with PSBT fields
new_threads_this_week.summary: - An anti-exfiltration protocol enables the host system to participate in nonce generation and verification.  - Two draft proposals introduce protocol details, new PSBT fields, and enhanced security via sign-to-contract tweaks.  - Implementations, testing tools, and resources exist, but formal cryptographic review and auditing remain outstanding.

new_threads_this_week.title: [Proposal] Tapleaf 0xc2: An overview of the Great Script Restoration (GSR)
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Five proposals introduce Tapleaf 0xc2, expanding Bitcoin Script with advanced scripting, introspection, and computational budgets.  - Backward compatibility, static analysis, and safety are maintained, with a comprehensive soft fork deployment strategy.  - Open questions include broader impacts, MEV concerns, segmented evaluation, flexible aggregation, and further standardization efforts.

new_threads_this_week.title: Full OP_RETURN value pruning
new_threads_this_week.summary: - satd introduces OP_RETURN data pruning with multiple configuration options, providing granular control for node operators.  - Pruning utilizes advanced system calls, impacts block serving, and may increase disk usage due to indexing.  - Customization options and reversibility ensure flexible management, with restoration preventing permanent data loss.

new_threads_this_week.title: Machine-checked soundness of BIP340 batch verification with 128-bit derived randomizers
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Formal proofs established soundness bounds for batch verification, highlighting strong security with 128-bit randomizers.  - Exploitation via grinding attacks is limited, with attacks requiring about 2^64 hashes for significant probability.  - A seed encoding issue exists unless message lengths are hashed; inclusion maintains result validity for arbitrary messages.

new_threads_this_week.title: Direct Messages (DMs)
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Efforts are being made to obtain user @neonrooks's npub for direct support.  - "Off the Chain" was recently added to btcplaylist.com, prompting this initiative.  - Alternatives are being explored since direct messaging is unavailable on the current forum.

new_threads_this_week.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Address compatibility issues occur due to inconsistent support for different cryptocurrency wallet address formats.  - Wallets must balance future-proofing with compatibility when choosing default address formats.  - Lack of comprehensive resources complicates user decisions and highlights the need for better communication and support.

new_threads_this_week.title: TULIP: Permissionless Decentralized Identity
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Decentralized identity systems use cryptographic keys and the Bitcoin blockchain for secure, pseudonymous authentication.  - Identity rotation is managed through a precommitted taproot chain, supporting recovery and enhancing security.  - Applications determine usage, with scalability ensured by minimal on-chain interactions and efficient transaction monitoring.

active_posts_this_week.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Relaying only stale headers is proposed to improve network transparency and minimize disruption to mining incentives.  - This approach boosts miner observability and revenue opportunities while slightly accelerating network convergence.  - Further changes, like relaying full block content, should follow careful evaluation of these initial results.

active_posts_this_week.title: [bitcoindev]
active_posts_this_week.summary:
- Version 2.1 introduces key updates, including fail-closed policy validation and explicit field requirements.
- Enhancements cover signed statement finality, finality-aware evidence, and corrections to k-of-n safety conditions.
- Outstanding issues include data serialization choice, incomplete wire schema, and lack of reference implementation.

active_posts_this_week.title: Great Consensus Cleanup Revival
active_posts_this_week.summary: - A patch to Bitcoin Core enforces the timewarp rule and provides detailed block validity logs.  - The adjustment enables efficient validation using a temporary data directory without affecting existing blockchain data.  - The approach detects and logs blocks with problematic timestamps, supporting further consensus rule analysis.

active_posts_this_week.title: Stats on compact block reconstructions
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Prefilling selected transactions in compact blocks enhances Bitcoin network relay efficiency and predictability.  - Experimental studies show prioritizing recently received mempool transactions effectively reduces the need for extra requests.  - Research suggests heuristics targeting previously missed transactions improve relay performance with less resource overhead.

active_posts_this_week.title: Public key recovery for EC leaves in P2MR (BIP-360)
active_posts_this_week.summary: - BIP342 introduces an accounting model considering both witness size and recovery operation costs.  - Benchmarks show Schnorr verification and recovery achieve similar speed with joint multiplication optimization.  - Elliptic curve recovery incurs lower CPU cost per weight than repeated-signature-check constructions in testing.

active_posts_this_week.title: TCP hole punching for Bitcoin nodes behind home NATs?
active_posts_this_week.summary: - CoreDev Tokyo 2026 explored TCP hole punching for improving Bitcoin Core peer connectivity behind NATs.  - Participants discussed technical challenges, NAT behaviors, and security risks of unsolicited incoming connections.  - Possible enhancements to peer discovery and connection mechanisms for greater robustness and decentralization were considered.

active_posts_this_week.title: Unspendable keys in descriptors
active_posts_this_week.summary: - A new pull request has been created to facilitate ongoing discussion about Bitcoin Improvement Proposals.  - The pull request and associated conversations are accessible online for public review and participation.  - Community members can provide feedback and follow the proposal's technical progress via this platform.

active_posts_this_week.title: Shielded Bitcoin: Private Transfers on the Bitcoin L1
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Repeated use of the same Bitcoin wallet can link transactions, risking user privacy.  - Strategies under consideration include using different wallets, CoinJoin, or intermediary services for obfuscation.  - Direct wallet payments lack privacy protections, making advanced mechanisms necessary for greater anonymity.

active_posts_this_week.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Colluding signers can manipulate points in a K-of-N scheme, but must all participate for updates.  - The VPSS1 protocol increases security, requiring all signers to confirm state and preventing equivocation.  - Storage demands and key management grow with group size, making the approach best for small groups.

active_posts_this_week.title: [BIP Draft] Co-signer Spending Policies
active_posts_this_week.summary: - The draft now features stricter verifier semantics, versioned commitments, and mechanisms for signed finality.  - Corrections have been made to the k-of-n component, with enhanced citations and section header updates.  - Full schema and reference implementation are unfinished, and community feedback is encouraged via mailing list or GitHub.

active_posts_this_week.title: Forwardable Peerswap Incentives, And Closing Surreptitious Communications Tunnels
active_posts_this_week.summary: - A robust hash-exchange protocol demands enforceable, on-chain commitments with clear guidelines for participant actions.  - Forwarders require confirmed Spilman channels before relaying, ensuring verifiable initiator commitment and incurring costs if aborted.  - Forwarders justify their fees by facilitating connections between nodes, leveraging their network intelligence and connectivity.

active_posts_this_week.title: Bitcoin Core v32.1 Released
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Version 32.1 binaries for x86_64 Linux have caused two unexpected restarts after deployment.  - These incidents suggest potential reliability and performance issues with the new release.  - Ongoing monitoring and investigation are advised to ensure optimal operation and prevent disruptions.
